g.ask.soft.text: Anything I can do for you?

g.ask.short.text: I haven't got it on me.

g.hook.warm.text: There you are. Come round the end of the counter a minute.

g.hook.dry.text: You. Stay a minute when you're done.

g.hook.old hand.text: Sit down a minute. I've got something for you.

g.hook.keen.text: Oh good, you're here. I've been saving something.

g.hook.precise.text: Have you got a minute? It's not for the board.

g.point.warm.text: {name} at {store} was asking after you. Wouldn't say what for.

g.point.dry.text: {name} over at {store} wants you. Don't ask me.

g.point.gruff.text: {name} at {store}. Go see. That's all I know.

g.point.old hand.text: {name} at {store} has been asking. Go on over when you're that way.

g.point.keen.text: {name} at {store} asked if you'd been in! Something's up.

g.point.precise.text: {name} at {store} would like to see you. No hurry, but don't forget.

g.pike.tell.1.text: There's a pike in Pipestone Bay as long as a paddle. My father hooked him in seventy-one and the line just went.

g.pike.tell.2.text: Oskar saw him last June, under the weeds at the mouth. First light or last. He takes something bright.

g.pike.go.text: Don't tell Oskar I told you.

g.pike.back.text: He's real. I had him in the canoe.

g.pike.thanks.1.text: You never! How long? No, don't, I'll cry. My father would have given his boat.

g.pike.thanks.2.text: That's from the jar we kept for whoever got him. Fifty years in a jar. Take it.

g.pike.page.1.text: Ruth: a pike in Pipestone Bay as long as a paddle. First light or last, something bright.

g.pike.page.2.text: Had him. At the boat he looked older than the bay.

g.laker.tell.1.text: Gabimichigami's deep at the east end. Two hundred feet. There's a laker down there older than this camp.

g.laker.tell.2.text: Early, in the morning, a spoon let all the way down. Slow. He'll think about it a long time.

g.laker.go.text: Bring me word. I don't need the fish.

g.laker.back.text: The old laker. I had him up.

g.laker.thanks.1.text: Well. I'll be. I had him on in sixty-eight and he took the spoon and my father's line both.

g.laker.thanks.2.text: That was my grandfather's spoon, the one before. It goes with whoever got him.

g.laker.page.1.text: Arvid: the old laker at the deep east end of Gabimichigami. Early, a spoon all the way down, slow.

g.laker.page.2.text: He came up out of the dark like a log.

g.laker.end.text: Arvid gave me his grandfather's spoon.

g.falls.tell.1.text: Okay, so. Off the west end of Pine Lake there's a creek you'd paddle right past.

g.falls.tell.2.text: Walk up it. Twenty minutes. There's a falls in there taller than the store and nobody ever goes.

g.falls.go.text: Get a picture! I've only ever heard about it.

g.falls.back.text: I found your falls. Here's the picture.

g.falls.thanks.1.text: Oh, look at that. It's real. It's going right over the till.

g.falls.thanks.2.text: Here. For the print. Don't argue.

g.falls.page.1.text: Thea: a creek off the west end of Pine Lake, a falls up it nobody walks to. A picture.

g.falls.page.2.text: The falls, taller than her store. It made its own wind.

g.falls.end.text: Thea has the falls over her till.

g.falls.first.text: The falls up from Pine Lake

g.cave.tell.1.text: You know the cliffs on Winchell, the north side? My uncle swore there's a hole in the wall you can stand up in.

g.cave.tell.2.text: Low, near the water, under a cedar. He said somebody left something in there a long time ago.

g.cave.go.text: Tell me what's in it. Promise!

g.cave.back.text: There is a cave on Winchell.

g.cave.thanks.1.text: There is! Oh, he'd be so smug. A kettle? A real trade kettle?

g.cave.thanks.2.text: No, you keep it. It came out because of you. Cook something in it for me.

g.cave.find.text: A copper kettle on a ledge, green with age, the bail still on.

g.cave.page.1.text: Lise: a hole in the north wall of Winchell, low, under a cedar. Her uncle's story.

g.cave.page.2.text: A copper kettle on a ledge in the dark. Somebody meant to come back for it.

g.cave.first.text: The hole in the Winchell wall

g.cabin.tell.1.text: There was a man trapped Cherokee in the thirties. Built himself a cabin in the back bays.

g.cabin.tell.2.text: Roof's gone, I'd think. My mother said he left with one coat on and a trunk behind.

g.cabin.thanks.1.text: Huh. Still standing. More than I can say for some places.

g.cabin.thanks.2.text: Wear the coat. He'd rather it went somewhere.

g.cabin.find.text: In the trunk, folded in newspaper from 1938: a red-and-black Mackinaw.

g.cabin.page.1.text: Bev: a trapper's cabin in the back bays of Cherokee, from the thirties. A trunk left behind.

g.cabin.page.2.text: Four log walls and the sky. The coat in the trunk smelled of cedar.

g.canoe.tell.1.text: My uncle put his canoe up on Ensign in fifty-four and never came back for it. Wood and canvas.

g.canoe.tell.2.text: North shore. Upside down in the brush. I looked twice. My knees don't look anymore.

g.canoe.go.text: If it's there, bring me the plate off the deck.

g.canoe.thanks.1.text: Huh. Seventy years under the brush.

g.canoe.thanks.2.text: Keep the plate. Here. Don't make it a thing.

g.canoe.find.text: A brass plate on the deck, the maker's name and a number. The canvas is gone to lace.

g.canoe.page.1.text: Gus: his uncle's wood-and-canvas canoe, put up on Ensign's north shore in 1954.

g.canoe.page.2.text: Under the brush, the ribs still round. I left it where it lay.

g.rookery.tell.1.text: Perent. The dead pines on the east side. Herons. Thirty nests, maybe.

g.rookery.tell.2.text: Spring into summer. Stay off the shore under them. Get a picture from the water.

g.rookery.go.text: From the water. I mean it.

g.rookery.back.text: I saw the herons on Perent.

g.rookery.thanks.2.text: For the print. The bird people pay me for a count; you did it.

g.rookery.page.1.text: Norm: herons in the dead pines on Perent. A picture from the water, not the shore.

g.rookery.page.2.text: Nests like brush piles in the tops, and the birds standing on them like sentries.

g.pine.tell.1.text: Lac La Croix. Above Boulder Bay, up the hill a bit. There's a white pine the loggers missed.

g.pine.tell.2.text: Biggest in the country. Walt knew it. Go put your arms round it.

g.pine.thanks.1.text: Couldn't reach round, could you. Nobody can.

g.pine.thanks.2.text: Here. Buy something that isn't from me.

g.pine.find.text: Your arms go a third of the way round. The bark is warm on the sun side.

g.pine.page.1.text: René: a white pine the loggers missed, above Boulder Bay on Lac La Croix. Walt knew it.

g.pine.page.2.text: My arms went a third of the way round.

g.pine.end.text: René said nobody can reach round.

g.pine.first.text: The big pine on Lac La Croix

g.summit.tell.1.text: Eagle Mountain is the highest point in the state. Two thousand three hundred and one feet.

g.summit.tell.2.text: The survey crew in thirty-eight left a tin under the cairn at the top. It should still be there.

g.summit.go.text: Put it back the way you found it.

g.summit.back.text: I found the tin on Eagle Mountain.

g.summit.thanks.1.text: Good. And you put the stone back.

g.summit.thanks.2.text: Here. For the climb. Write your name in the book next time.

g.summit.find.text: Under the top stone, a tobacco tin. A folded note inside, in pencil. You copy it into your book and put the tin back.

g.summit.page.1.text: Merle: a survey tin under the cairn on top of Eagle Mountain, left in 1938.

g.summit.page.2.text: A note in pencil in a tobacco tin. I put it back.

g.summit.end.text: Merle said write your name next time.

g.survey.text: U.S.C.&G.S. party, August 1938. Benchmark set. Clear and cold, wind NW. Eat your lunch, the view won't wait.

g.spring.tell.1.text: On Duncan, the north shore, there's a spring comes right out of the rock. Cold as January.

g.spring.tell.2.text: Somebody hung a tin cup on a nail there before I was born. My mother drank from it.

g.spring.back.text: I drank from the spring on Duncan.

g.spring.thanks.1.text: Isn't it the coldest water you ever had? And the cup?

g.spring.thanks.2.text: You keep it with you. Hang another one there next time you go by.

g.spring.find.text: A blue enamel cup on a nail in a cedar, chipped at the rim. The water aches in your teeth.

g.spring.page.1.text: Inga: a spring out of the rock on Duncan's north shore, a tin cup on a nail.

g.spring.page.2.text: The coldest water I ever had.

g.spring.end.text: Inga says hang another cup there.

g.berries.tell.1.text: The old burn above Big Moose. Every August it's blue up there. Nobody picks it but the bears.

g.berries.tell.2.text: Bring me some and I'll bake. That's the deal.

g.berries.go.text: Make noise up there. The bears know about it too.

g.berries.back.text: I picked the burn above Big Moose.

g.berries.thanks.1.text: Oh, look at those. The little wild ones. Give me an hour.

g.berries.thanks.2.text: There. A whole pie. Don't you share it with anybody you don't like.

g.berries.find.text: Wild blueberries, small and dark, under the black snags.

g.berries.page.1.text: Joanne: blueberries every August on the old burn above Big Moose. Make noise.

g.berries.page.2.text: Blue under the black snags. I ate as many as I kept.

g.cold.warm.text: Prices went up. I'm sorry. I'm not, really.

g.cold.dry.text: Prices went up. You can afford it.

g.cold.old hand.text: It's the same gear. It's a different price for you.

g.cold.keen.text: Um. The prices are, um. Different now. For you.

g.cold.precise.text: Your prices changed. You know why.

g.soft.31.ask.text: The fire department keeps a coffee can on the counter. Forty dollars wouldn't hurt you.

g.soft.31.done.text: That'll buy a lot of hose. Your money's the same as anybody's here now.

g.soft.25.ask.text: Somebody left a mess at a site out there. Go and pack it out.

g.soft.25.job.text: Bring it all back. All of it.

g.soft.25.done.text: Fine. We're square. Same prices as the rest.

g.soft.38.ask.text: There's a site somebody's been complaining about. Go and look at it for me. Tell me straight.

g.soft.38.done.text: Huh. Thanks. Your prices are back, since you're wondering.

g.soft.51.ask.text: The kitchen wants a laker and I'm too old to go. Bring me one, cold.

g.soft.51.done.text: That's a fish. All right. You pay what everybody pays.

g.soft.64.ask.text: I'm supposed to do a loon count and I can't leave the store. Could you? Please?

g.soft.64.done.text: You did it! Okay. Normal prices. I never liked the other ones.

g.soft.16.ask.text: I need a water reading on a lake out there. The disk is under the counter. Do it properly.

g.soft.16.job.text: Shade side of the canoe. Write it down.

g.soft.16.done.text: Thank you. That's clean work. Your prices are the ordinary prices again.

g.soft.1.ask.text: The rescue squad's raising for a new boat. Sixty dollars. You know what a boat's for.

g.soft.1.done.text: That's good of you. We're even, you and me.

g.soft.6.ask.text: The bookmobile lost its funding. There's a jar. Twenty-five dollars, if you can.

g.soft.6.done.text: Oh, bless you. Come here. And the prices are back where they were, for you.

g.soft.12.ask.text: Go and walk a carry for me and tell me what's down on it. I don't trust the forest service's word.

g.soft.12.done.text: Good. You pay what you used to.

g.soft.36.ask.text: Beavers are at it again out there. Go and look at the dam and tell me how high.

g.soft.36.job.text: Don't pull it apart. Just look.

g.soft.36.done.text: Well. You're useful. Prices are back.

g.soft.40.ask.text: There's a tree down somewhere it shouldn't be. Find it. Report it properly.

g.soft.40.job.text: Where, how big, which way it fell.

g.soft.40.done.text: Good report. I've put you back on the ordinary prices.

g.soft.49.ask.text: The school's bus fund. There's a jar. Fifty dollars would get them a long way.

g.soft.49.done.text: Oh, that's kind. You're family here again. Same prices as everyone.

g.soft.67.ask.text: Talk to the people out there about their fish. Counts and sizes. The state wants it and I don't.

g.soft.67.job.text: Write it down. They lie a little.

g.soft.69.ask.text: Could you go and check on a site for me? It's a long way, I know. I'd owe you!

g.soft.69.done.text: You went all that way. Okay. Normal prices. Like before.
